summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by emotional stress and missed insulin. She presented with severe nausea, vomiting, and anxiety after a family conflict. Treatment included an insulin drip and IV fluids, with resolution of DKA. Her nausea improved slowly, and she resumed oral intake. The Lantus dose was reduced to 25 units at discharge to prevent hypoglycemia. She was counseled to avoid non-prescribed narcotics, which could worsen gastroparesis and glycemic control. Social work and mental health support were recommended due to recurrent admissions linked to stress and depression. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans.
